_comment: Reviewed verification recipes for scripts/register-secret-verified.sh --recipe <name> (claude-code-skills#478). A recipe lands only by PR, with the provider's documented behaviour cited in its evidence field. Network recipes must carry a negative control: the same request with a wrong value must answer differently, or nothing is stored. Behaviour that can only be measured with a real value (the provider's answer to a wrong client secret) is measured by that control on every run, and the first real run's answers are the ledger row's detail. Never add a recipe that stores without a check.

access-service-token.evidence: Cloudflare Rotate a service token API: POST accounts/{account_id}/access/service_tokens/{service_token_id}/rotate. previous_client_secret_expires_at is explicit because omission expires the old secret immediately. Preserve its original expires_at until Router release smoke. The exact existing token, reusable Service Auth policy, four public destinations and unique application were read back from the company account on 2026-11-01. Every run rechecks the full application inventory and policies, then requires four HTTP403 wrong-secret controls and four HTTP200 OpenAI models JSON responses without redirects. https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/zero_trust/subresources/access/subresources/service_tokens/methods/rotate/

access-service-token-recovery.evidence: Recover only the same pair retained by the reviewed rotation recipe after a refused probe or partial GitHub registration. Never POST or rotate. Bind the owner-only saved result and required timestamps to the current service-token metadata and preserved original expiry, then repeat the complete four-origin configuration and negative-control/real JSON checks before the existing store. The original recovery remains untouched until audited GitHub readback. https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/zero_trust/subresources/access/subresources/service_tokens/methods/rotate/

github-oauth.evidence: GitHub REST 2022-11-28, Check a token: Basic auth with client_id / client_secret; 'Invalid tokens will return 404 NOT FOUND'. The control counts only a definite authentication failure, 401, as 'the endpoint told the wrong secret apart'. GitHub does not document the answer to a wrong client secret (only 200 / 404 / 422 are listed), so a first run that answers anything else refuses and is itself the measurement (M1). No answer, 403, 429, 5xx or a non-JSON body is inconclusive for both requests.

slack-oauth.evidence: Slack oauth.v2.access: Basic auth recommended; errors invalid_client_id / bad_client_secret / invalid_code are documented. The control counts only bad_client_secret, a definite authentication failure; the order of Slack's checks is not documented, so the first run is the measurement (M2). No answer, 403, 429, 5xx or a non-JSON body is inconclusive for both requests.

mcp-token.evidence: cor-os packages/computer-mcp/src/index.ts authorize(): 'Bearer <MCP_TOKEN>' is compared exactly, so no provider can verify it; release-secrets.mjs boundedSecret: at most 256 KiB. packages/computer-mcp/README.md: the administrator's UAT uses the MCP Bearer, so the value is also kept in Bitwarden (the env ledger), never shown.

intake-keys.evidence: cor-os docs/publishing-corpus.md:134-141 and release-secrets.mjs validatePublishingIntakeKeys: 4 distinct 32-byte keys plus revisions in canonical order. The generator and the check are the consumer's own commands (cor-os#126); until cor-os has them the recipe refuses.
